previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with fibrosing mesenteritis, multiple abdominal surgeries, and chronic pain, was admitted after a fall that worsened a chronic left ankle avulsion fracture. She presented with severe ankle pain, swelling, and a supratherapeutic INR of 12.3, requiring vitamin K and FFP. During admission, she developed a partial small bowel obstruction likely exacerbated by narcotic use, managed conservatively with NPO status, G-tube suction, TPN, and octreotide. Her INR initially dropped but was successfully re-anticoagulated with warfarin 7.5mg daily, bridged with Lovenox. Levothyroxine was increased to 88mcg due to elevated TSH. Anemia remained stable, and no active bleeding was confirmed. She improved with dietary advancement, discontinued TPN, and was discharged home ambulating with a CAM walker, on updated medication regimens with close outpatient follow-up for INR and thyroid function.

outpatient appointments.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ with nausea, vomiting and diarrhea, concern for
partial small-bowel obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to abdominal radiograph performed on ___ and CT abdomen and pelvis performed ___.

FINDINGS:  Two frontal radiographs of the abdomen demonstrate a normal bowel
gas pattern with no evidence of obstruction, free air or pneumatosis.  The
gastric tube is again identified and unchanged in position.  Surgical clips
overlying the right upper quadrant are noted.  Stable positioning of a spinal
bone stimulator.

IMPRESSION:  Normal bowel gas pattern.  No evidence of obstruction.

INDICATION:  ___ female with recurrent partial small bowel
obstruction.  Request for routine G-tube exchange.

RADIOLOGIST:  The procedure was performed by Dr. ___.  The attending,
Dr. ___ was present and supervised the entire study.

ANESTHESIA:  Topical lidocaine gel was used for local anesthesia.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:

After explaining the risks, benefits and alternatives of the procedure,
written informed consent was obtained.  The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the angiographic table.  The upper
abdomen including the indwelling gastrostomy catheter were prepped and draped
in the usual sterile fashion.  A preprocedure huddle and a timeout was
performed per ___ protocol.  A scout fluoroscopic image was obtained showing
the indwelling gastrostomy tube optimally placed within the stomach.  The
catheter was cut near the hub and then 0.035 straight ___ wire was passed
beyond its tip and coiled in the stomach.  The catheter was then removed over
the wire and exchanged for a similar new 12 ___ ___ catheter.  On
obtaining adequate positioning within the stomach, the wire was removed and
the catheter was pigtailed and locked.  Contrast was injected to confirm its
position within the stomach.

Silver nitrate was then used to cauterize the prominent granulation tissue
around the tube insertion site.  Sterile dressings were applied.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well with no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:

Uncomplicated exchange of existing gastrostomy catheter for a new 12 ___
___ gastrostomy tube with tip positioned in the gastric lumen.  The
catheter is ready for use.

INDICATION:  ___ female with previous abdominal surgeries, presents
with abdominal pain.  Evaluate for dilatation of small bowel loops.

COMPARISON:  Upright abdominal radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:

Two abdominal radiographs show several bowel air-fluid levels and a otherwise
normal bowel gas pattern without dilation of loops of small bowel.  There is
no evidence of obstruction, free air or pneumatosis.  The gastric tube is
again identified, in unchanged position.  Surgical clips overlying the right
upper quadrant consistent with cholecystectomy are seen.  There is unchanged
position of the spinal nerve stimulator.  There is air distally in the rectum.

IMPRESSION:

Normal bowel gas pattern.  No evidence of obstruction.
